Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied from 2017-09-21

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and regulations; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 2.1 and s. 21.1 (register of individuals with significant control); Bill C-42, S.C. 2024, c. 15 (public beneficial ownership registry upon proclamation); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46 money-laundering offences; FINTRAC guidance and administrative monetary penalty regime.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (corporate register of individuals with significant control maintained at registered office; accessible to law enforcement, CRA, and FINTRAC on lawful demand; transition to a publicly searchable registry expected upon proclamation of Bill C-42)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status of the foreign parent entity issued by the home-jurisdiction corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the parent entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention, in force for Canada since 2024-01-11), or consular legalization where the home jurisdiction is not a Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the foreign parent's constitutional documents (certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, and bylaws)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction corporate registry or registered agent authorized to certify corporate records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by certified English/French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized identification and address dossier for each UBO, director, and officer (passport, national identity document, proof of residential address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notarial act (or consular authentication at the Canadian embassy/consulate for non-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign parent authorizing incorporation of the Canadian subsidiary, appointment of initial directors, and execution authority for the registered agent/in-house counsel agreements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company secretary or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization with certified translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, senior officers, and counterparties against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List (SEMA and United Nations Act), and domestic/international PEP databases; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and non-face-to-face incorporations; FINTRAC record-keeping, reporting, and suspicious transaction reporting duties under the PCMLTFA; risk-based re-screening at least annually and upon any material ownership or control change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and Federal Corporate Name Search (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada / ISED; https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/125.nsf/eng/home)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names must contain a distinctive element and a legal element (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporée'); names may be in English, French, or bilingual; a name in a third language is acceptable only when transliterated in Roman characters; the proposed name must not be confusing with any existing federal or provincial name under the NUANS search doctrine (CBCA ss. 10-12 and incorporation regulations).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Federal name search reports remain valid for 90 days and are not extendable; upon expiry the applicant must procure a new name search report and re-file. If the Director of Corporations rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Director General, Corporations Canada within 30 days, attaching the original name search report, a revised proposed name (if any), and legal arguments on non-confusion; failed reconsideration may be pursued by judicial review before the Federal Court under section 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, or incorporation may proceed under a numbered name with a later amendment to change the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in practice for a CBCA corporation, provided the virtual-office provider maintains a physical street address in the province designated in the articles, accepts service of process during normal business hours, and does not use a post-office box; the register of individuals with significant control and corporate records must be physically available at the registered office; virtual offices are generally accepted for a low-risk, non-public-facing EOR staffing service corporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Corporations Canada registered-office inspections are rare (under 2% annual probability for a low-risk service entity); combined CRA and provincial employment/payroll compliance audit probability is estimated at 10-15% within the first 36 months of operation; commercial substance records (board minutes, service agreements, payroll trust accounts, UBO register) must be contemporaneously maintained.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for FINTRAC-compliant corporate CDD/EDD packages; flat per-entity fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-jurisdiction notarial and apostille authorities; Global Affairs Canada authentication services (if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Global Affairs Canada apostille fee C$15 per document; notary tariffs vary by jurisdiction; certified translation at market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and corporate agent/service-of-process representative, first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for federal CBCA registered office and agent services; statutory obligation under CBCA section 19

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing blended hourly rate (C$350-C$450 per hour) or fixed-fee incorporation package; market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provincial extra-provincial registration and employment-recruiter licensing coordination where applicable (Ontario, British Columbia, or Alberta)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial corporate registries (e.g., Ontario Business Registry, BC Corporate Online, Alberta Corporate Registry) and provincial recruiter licensing authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provincial registration and licensing tariffs (e.g., Ontario Employment Standards Act 2000 recruiter licence C$250-C$750 depending on scope); market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CRA business number, GST/HST, payroll (PD7A), and EOR payroll trust account registration coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and applicable provincial licensing authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No federal statutory fee for CRA Business Number registration; professional coordination fee and applicable provincial licensing tariff; market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C., 1985, c. C-44, as amended; incorporation and governance provisions under Part 2 (ss. 5-20) and corporate records in s. 106; Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) and Initial Registered Office Address and First Directors (Form 4002) filed through the Corporations Canada online registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; no escrow requirement. Shares may be issued for cash, property or past services at director-determined amounts, and one class of no-par common shares is standard for an EOR platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accept the initial share subscriptions tendered by the persons named in the capital schedule and issue the corresponding common shares for the stated consideration; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be fixed at the municipal address set out in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the minute book and statutory records be kept at that office; RESOLVED, that the following individuals are appointed as officers, until successors are elected or appointed: President, Corporate Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, with authority to execute banking, payroll, and employment-services documents; and RESOLVED, that management is authorized to take necessary actions to activate the corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada online filing portal and NUANS-authorized service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary name search through a Corporations Canada authorized service provider or the Corporations Canada online portal. Select a distinctive corporate name containing a mandatory legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., or Canada Inc.; secure a date-stamped NUANS report to accompany the incorporation filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing with an existing trademark or corporate name, file a revised name request with a new NUANS report or proceed under a numbered company name (e.g., 12345678 Canada Inc.) and register a separate trade name after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles and Initial Registered Office Information
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada; corporate counsel or licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 4001 Articles of Incorporation and Form 4002 Initial Registered Office Address and First Directors. Define authorized capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, any permitted business restrictions, and appoint the first director(s). Identify the municipal address for the registered office and confirm the first director consents are executed.
required_dossiers: Form 4002 Initial Registered Office Address and First Directors
Consent to Act as First Director
Share structure and class rights summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada returns an error or query, correct the affected article or director information and resubmit through the online filing portal before the fee is processed; respond to any formal requisition within the stated deadline to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the final Form 4001 and Form 4002 through Corporations Canada's internet incorporation service, pay the statutory filing fee, and receive the electronic Certificate of Incorporation with the federal corporation number. The filing may be made in English or French and becomes effective on the date shown on the certificate.
required_dossiers: NUANS report where a name is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried after submission, use the Corporations Canada error-correction route to file corrected articles online or by registered mail; statutory fees are generally non-refundable if the application is abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Establishment, Corporate Records and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada; corporate secretary or registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the registered office address stated in the Certificate of Incorporation; create the corporate minute book, securities register, register of directors, and register of shareholders; issue the subscribed common shares in accordance with the first board resolution and record share consideration in the corporate books.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and share ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada identifies a missing or defective record, file the required amendment or supplementary form (e.g., change of registered office or director change) and maintain current records at the registered office to avoid delinquency proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt general corporate by-laws covering board meetings, quorum, signing authority, banking resolutions, indemnification and share transfers. Pass a board resolution appointing the President, Corporate Secretary and Chief Financial Officer, and authorize designated officers to execute payroll, banking and employment-services contracts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a by-law or appointment is later challenged or contains an irregularity, the directors may pass a confirmatory resolution, ratify the prior act, and file relevant amendments where required by the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Number, Tax Registrations and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with CRA to obtain a federal Business Number and enroll the required program accounts, including GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll source-deductions. Confirm the registered office address and filing language; set up payroll remittance schedules and authorized accountant or payroll administrator access.
required_dossiers: Payroll remittance and tax appointment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA suspends or queries the registration, update program account information through the CRA Business Portal or call Corporations/Business Registration; provide a signed letter of authorization to the appointed tax representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employment Agency and Physical Premises Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) and applicable provincial Ministry of Labour or Employment Standards office; local municipal fire and building departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for any applicable employment agency or private staffing licence in the province(s) of operation; register for ESDC employer compliance where foreign workers are engaged; obtain fire safety and occupancy clearance for the head office; confirm payroll liability insurance and workers' compensation account registration.
required_dossiers: Commercial lease or proof of premises
Fire code compliance and occupancy certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence application is refused or queried, provide supplementary corporate and payroll compliance documentation to the provincial licensing tribunal or ESDC; request interim authorization where statutory appeal deadlines apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) – Temporary Foreign Worker Program and Federal Labour Standards; provincial Ministry of Labour / Employment Standards office where an employment agency licence is required
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Employer Compliance Registration (ESDC) and, where applicable, provincial Employment Agency Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / Impact Assessment Agency of Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – administrative office and EOR back-office service; not a designated project under the Impact Assessment Act; no full Environmental Impact Assessment or registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharges, VOC emissions or hazardous waste generation; adhere to municipal waste handling and building code requirements; any emergency generator or HVAC emissions must meet provincial air quality and National Fire Code standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Head-office fire safety certification and occupancy load inspection by the local fire marshal; compliance with structural and building code requirements; workplace health and safety clearance under the applicable occupational health and safety statutes, including the Canada Labour Code Part II for federally regulated employment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — CRA My Business Account, Business Registration Online (BRO), GST/HST NETFILE; Corporations Canada for federal incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian federal Business Corporation obtains its Business Number (BN) automatically upon federal incorporation and filing of the initial corporate income tax return; the CRA simultaneously issues the corporate tax program account (RC). Where a non-resident entity has not incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act, tax registration is effected by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) or through Business Registration Online. The registrant must then open separate program accounts for GST/HST (RT), payroll deductions (RP), and corporate income tax (RC) as applicable. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada are required to obtain a BN and may be required to designate a Canadian resident representative for CRA correspondence and statutory notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. I-5). Resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident corporations are taxed on Canadian-source business income and certain Canadian-source passive income, subject to Part I tax, Part XIII withholding tax, and the Part I branch tax applicable to non-resident corporations operating in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box or disregarded-entity election comparable to the United States regime; entity classification is determined by CRA administrative practice, corporate law, and the Income Tax Act. Available statutory elections relevant to cross-border operations include the ITA section 216 election, under which a non-resident may elect to file a Canadian return and pay Part I tax on net Canadian rental income instead of Part XIII gross-basis withholding, and certain treaty-based elections to reduce branch tax. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Canadian anti-hybrid and anti-avoidance rules apply under the Income Tax Act and the Excise Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. E-15)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies but excluding exempt supplies) in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for the small supplier threshold; non-residents with a permanent establishment or deemed carrying-on-business activity in Canada may be required to register even below this threshold. Voluntary registration is available for persons making taxable supplies in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no federal real-time fiscal invoice clearance, API stamping, or mandatory digital seal regime for GST/HST invoices. A GST/HST registrant must issue a valid tax invoice containing prescribed information, including supplier name, CRA Business Number and GST/HST account number, invoice date, description of supply, tax status (taxable, zero-rated, exempt), and consideration paid. Electronic invoicing is permitted, including B2B EDI, XML, or PEPPOL formats; however, CRA does not pre-clear invoices. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically by registrants whose annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1.5 million, and T4/T4A payroll information returns are subject to mandatory electronic filing. Quebec maintains a separate provincial electronic invoicing and centralized registration environment that is distinct from the federal GST/HST system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, supplies of goods exported by the supplier are zero-rated where the goods are delivered outside Canada within the prescribed statutory period and the supplier retains proof of export. Supplies of services to non-resident persons are zero-rated under section 23 of Part V unless the service relates to real property situated in Canada, relates to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or is supplied to an individual while the individual is physically in Canada. For a Global EOR / cross-border contractor payroll provider, zero-rating is available where the recipient is a non-resident and the employer-of-record, payroll administration, compliance, and workforce management services are not connected to Canadian real property or tangible personal property physically situated in Canada and are not direct services rendered to an individual present in Canada. The supplier must maintain contemporaneous documentation establishing the non-resident status of the recipient, the place of supply, and the nature of the services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export report / cargo declaration, including Form B13A where applicable
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical export of goods from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or wire/ACH bank records establishing receipt of foreign-source funds from the non-resident recipient
Signed service agreement or purchase order with the non-resident client
Non-resident status evidence, such as a foreign tax residency certificate, foreign business registration document, or sworn declaration
Commercial invoice identifying the supply as zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims and overstated input tax credit refunds are subject to CRA reassessment, cancellation of refunds, denial of input tax credits, and retroactive clawback of previously allowed non-resident refunds. Statutory penalties apply for false statements and omissions in GST/HST filings, including the greater of a fixed amount and a percentage of understated net tax, and gross-negligence penalties of up to 50% of the amount assessed; interest is compounded daily. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act may result in fines of up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment, and directors or officers may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid GST/HST amounts where they authorized or acquiesced in the false claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted convertibility for both current account transactions and capital movements. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior approval or surrender obligations. No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is required; foreign currency earnings may be retained in offshore accounts or converted at market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory surrender of export proceeds applies. Exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds offshore or convert to CAD at prevailing market rates. All foreign exchange transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC. Certain goods exports may require permits under the Export and Import Permit Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for licensed fintech EMI providers such as Wise Business or Mercury, subject to full Canadian AML/KYC compliance, FINTRAC registration where required, and adherence to provincial money services business regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding and KYC verification is fully permitted for Canadian federal corporations. Directors must complete video identification and beneficial ownership verification; physical presence is not mandated for entities with complete corporate documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry search, shareholder register, and FINTRAC-compliant beneficial ownership declaration

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for capital injection or operational deposits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, audited financial statements, board resolutions, and tax filings confirming legitimate business purpose

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EOR contractor payroll and cross-border disbursement verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employment contracts, payroll registers, proof of foreign labor law compliance, and platform agreements

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose codes such as 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. All wires require supporting documentation including incorporation certificate, board resolution authorizing the injection, and source-of-funds evidence. Transactions above FINTRAC thresholds must be reported.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements cleared through SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 rules. EOR payroll disbursements supported via direct bank transfers or licensed payment platforms compliant with Canadian payment rails and tax withholding requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution. The CBCA also provides for offence penalties for filing failures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within six months after each taxation year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties generally apply when tax is owing; unpaid balances accrue interest. Repeated failures may increase penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Information Filing and Register Review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submit required ISC information with the annual return; file changes within 15 days after the corporation becomes aware of them.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may constitute an offence and can result in fines or imprisonment for responsible individuals; Corporations Canada may also take compliance action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general revenue or asset threshold applies under the CBCA. A distributing corporation must appoint an auditor. A non-distributing corporation may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution, subject to statutory conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises are generally available to private corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain an ISC register and take reasonable steps to confirm and update its information at least annually. File prescribed ISC information with the annual return and report changes to Corporations Canada within 15 days after becoming aware of them. Record share transfers and update the register of members promptly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book and directors' and shareholders' resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 0–1,000 annually; the corporation must maintain a registered office in its governing jurisdiction, but a separate registered-agent appointment is generally not required.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 5,000–25,000 or more annually, depending on complexity, locations, and transaction volume; no statutory audit is required where a qualifying non-distributing corporation validly dispenses with one.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act s.123: 38% base less 10% provincial abatement less 13% general rate reduction), plus applicable provincial/territorial corporate tax (e.g., Ontario 11.5%, producing a combined Ontario-based headline rate of approximately 26.5%; Alberta 8%, producing a combined rate of 23%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) may claim the Small Business Deduction (s.125) reducing the federal rate to 9% on up to CAD 500,000 of active business income per associated group, with the business limit phased out where taxable capital exceeds CAD 10 million; the Manufacturing and Processing Profits Deduction (s.125.1) and SR&ED investment tax credits (s.127) are available but rarely material for an EOR payroll model; the general rate reduction under s.123.4 applies to active business income not eligible for the SBD, resulting in a 15% effective statutory federal rate for scale operations.
